title: docs(skills,adr): app-composition.md and ADR-0055 still teach a 'recordId -> filters -> viewName' precedence the spec REFUSES (sites objectui#8563 could not reach)
body:
## Measured

Found while chaining the spec's `objectNavTargetExclusivity` into `NavigationItemSchema` (objectui#8563). That card scoped the doc correction to the `.describe()` on `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`; two more sites teach the same sentence and are outside that card's file surface.

On `origin/main` `a650bb356`, a repo-wide sweep for a precedence claim naming these fields (control: 544 lines mention "precedence" repo-wide excluding CHANGELOGs, so the instrument is not selecting on emptiness) leaves exactly two sites uncorrected:

- `skills/objectui/guides/app-composition.md`, "Contract Reminders (spec-strict)":
  `- Object-item target precedence: recordId -> filters -> viewName`
- `docs/adr/0055-parameterized-bare-data-surface.md`, item 5:
  `Precedence within type:'object': recordId -> filters -> viewName.`

## Why this is a metadata trap, not a doc nit

There is no precedence. `@objectstack/spec`'s `objectNavTargetExclusivity` — verified against the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` tarball, not upstream `main` — REFUSES `filters` combined with `recordId` or `viewName`, and `runAction` combined with `recordId`. The spec's own `filters` describe reads `Mutually exclusive with recordId/viewName.`

So an author who follows the sentence writes a document that is refused. Before objectui#8563 that refusal happened at publish; after it, `NavigationItemSchema.safeParse` refuses it here too.

The skill file is the sharp end: `skills/objectui/guides/app-composition.md` is published guidance an AI reads *in order to author navigation metadata*. It is a table of nav shapes followed by "Contract Reminders (spec-strict)" — the precedence line sits under a heading that asserts it is the strict contract, while being the one line the strict contract refuses.

## Why it was not fixed in the objectui#8563 PR

Deliberately held, not overlooked:

- `skills/**` is a customer-published skill package. Touching it pulls in `check:skills-paths`, `check:skill-examples` and `check:skill-eval-tokens` plus the published-skill line-budget accounting — a verification surface the schema card does not otherwise open.
- An ADR is a decision record. Amending one after the fact is a maintainer's call, not a rider on a schema PR. ADR-0055's item 5 may want a correction, an amendment note, or nothing at all — that is a judgement this seat should not make silently.

Both were reported rather than edited. Priority and labels belong to this repo's seats.

## Suggested shape

Replace the precedence claim with the refusal in both places, matching the spec's own wording (`Mutually exclusive with recordId/viewName.`), and in the skill note the two asymmetries the rule keeps on purpose, since a "make them all exclusive" correction would be wrong: `recordId` + `viewName` is TOLERATED, and `runAction` is refused with `recordId` only — it composes with `viewName` or `filters`.

Related but NOT the same file surface: `packages/layout/src/__tests__/resolveHref.test.ts` names the precedence in a test title. That one describes real, deliberate RUNTIME fallback behaviour in `resolveHref` for documents that predate the guard, and is accurate as such — it is noted here so a sweep does not "correct" a renderer's defensive path into a second rejection point.
